title: Odd-parity magnon spin polarization from chiral four-spin exchange in a honeycomb antiferromagnet
abstract: Chiral four-spin exchange generates a momentum-dependent magnon spin in a compensated honeycomb antiferromagnet at zero magnetic field. For a Néel vector tilted by an angle $θ_0$ from the layer normal, the interaction contributes to intersublattice magnon pairing already at harmonic order, with an amplitude proportional to $\cosθ_0\sin^2θ_0$. Biaxial anisotropy mixes the two longitudinal-spin sectors, producing nonquantized mode spins that are odd in momentum, while a sublattice-exchange relation keeps the magnon energies reciprocal. A temperature gradient then induces a spin density along the Néel axis through a redistribution of magnon occupations. Reversing the four-spin coupling reverses this spin density and the mode spins without changing the magnon energies. MnPS$_3$ motivates the magnetic geometry; realizing the interaction requires a structural modification compatible with the symmetry assumptions of the model.
summary: This theoretical work investigates how chiral four-spin exchange generates an odd-parity magnon spin in a honeycomb antiferromagnet. By analyzing the magnon spectrum and calculating the thermal spin accumulation response, the authors show that this interaction leads to a measurable spin density change proportional to the temperature gradient. This work provides insight into spin-momentum locking mechanisms in frustrated magnetic insulators.
main_problem: The study aims to determine the microscopic interactions responsible for generating an odd-parity magnon spin polarization in a compensated honeycomb antiferromagnet while maintaining a reciprocal magnon energy spectrum.
main_result: Chiral four-spin exchange generates an odd-parity magnon spin, and a temperature gradient induces a measurable spin density along the Néel axis that reverses sign upon reversing the four-spin coupling.
method: The analysis employs a spin-wave expansion using Holstein-Primakoff bosons to diagonalize the quadratic Hamiltonian derived from the full spin model.
model_or_system: The system is a honeycomb antiferromagnet, motivated by MnPS3, modeled with spins on two sublattices (A and B). The Hamiltonian includes nearest-neighbor exchange and a chiral four-spin interaction term.
key_observables: Odd-parity magnon spin ($	ext{L}_{n\mathbf{q}}$), magnon energies ($E_{1,2}(\mathbf{q})$), and the thermally induced spin density ($\delta s_L$).

main_assumptions: The analysis is restricted to the harmonic approximation (quadratic Hamiltonian), and the calculation of thermal spin accumulation assumes well-defined quasiparticles.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the model geometry, the momentum-odd nature of the magnon spin ($	ext{L}_{1\mathbf{q}}$), and the temperature dependence of the thermal spin accumulation coefficient ($\chi_y$).
paper_structure: The paper develops the Hamiltonian, solves the bosonic eigenvalue problem to find magnon energies and spins, and then uses the relaxation-time approximation to calculate the non-equilibrium thermal spin accumulation response.
why_interesting: The study connects lattice geometry (honeycomb structure) and specific higher-order spin interactions (chiral four-spin exchange) to measurable transport properties (thermal spin current), which is relevant for understanding spin-charge conversion in magnetic materials.
